1.x: **New direction:** as the Roman market was lost, Indian merchants relied more on **South-East Asian trade** – it did not revive the northern economy.
**Silk weavers:** a guild left Lata (Gujarat) for **Mandsaur** (mid-5th c.) and took up other professions – a sign of falling silk demand.
**Gradual decline of towns:** a feature of the **Gupta period**; **Pataliputra** had become a village when Hiuen-Tsang came.

**Post-Gupta decline of trade:** towns such as **Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, Kaushambi** declined, with a **paucity of coins**; the decline was marked from the 6th–7th c., well before the middle of the 9th century.
**R.S. Sharma's view:** shrinking towns, self-reliant villages, few gold coins – the basis of the **urban decay and feudalism** thesis; critics note coins still appear in texts and inscriptions.

4.x: **Mission:** to **visit Buddhist institutions and collect copies of Buddhist manuscripts**; he never named the king.
**Hospital:** a **free hospital at Pataliputra**, endowed by citizens – poor patients got doctors, food and medicine.

**Dates and route:** **c. 399–412 CE** (Chandragupta II); came overland via Central Asia and Gandhara, returned by sea via **Tamralipti** (port of departure) and **Sri Lanka**; account = **Fo-kwo-ki** ("Record of Buddhist Kingdoms").
